schema: organisations and people who can surface land or clear a path. tier 1 = highest acres reachable per hour.

contacts.role: Economic development arm of ~250 Iowa utilities — 150+ rural electric cooperatives, municipal utilities, independent broadband
contacts.ask: Every 300+ acre site their member utilities know of, listed or not, in the screen counties — plus which county boards are receptive.
contacts.why: Already appears twice in the CoStar export as the listing contact on the Mona Rail Site and the Iowa Falls industrial site. Both a live broker relationship and the door into 250 utilities.

contacts.org: Mid Iowa Growth Partnership / Greater Fort Dodge Growth Alliance
contacts.role: Regional partnership covering nine counties
contacts.web: midiowagrowth.com · 24 N 9th St, Suite A, Fort Dodge, IA 50501
contacts.counties: Calhoun · Hamilton · Hardin · Humboldt · Kossuth · Palo Alto · Pocahontas · Webster · Wright
contacts.ask: Full land inventory over 300 acres across all nine counties, county-by-county ordinance posture, and which cities hold adoptable 427B ordinances and existing urban renewal areas.
contacts.why: Their nine-county footprint covers the top of the screen almost exactly, including Kossuth, which ranks first.

contacts.org: Mid Iowa Growth Partnership / Greater Fort Dodge Growth Alliance
contacts.role: Chief executive, same nine-county region
contacts.ask: Escalation path if the economic development director cannot move a county board.
contacts.why: Second contact at the same organisation — use only if the first stalls.

contacts.role: Certified Sites programme, regional business development managers, High Quality Jobs Program
contacts.web: opportunityiowa.gov · 1963 Bell Ave, Suite 200, Des Moines, IA 50315
contacts.ask: Complete certified-site register filtered above 300 acres, the regional business development manager for each screen county, and any confidential large-site inventory.
contacts.why: Mills Crossings Mega Site at Glenwood is 1,600+ acres with due diligence already completed.

contacts.role: Economic development and surplus real estate
contacts.ask: Industrial site inventory, certified sites, and non-operating or former generation land held as surplus.
contacts.why: In this channel the utility is the landowner, not the supplier.

contacts.role: Economic development and industrial land
contacts.ask: Industrial site inventory and surplus land, starting with capacity remaining at Big Cedar Industrial Center.
contacts.why: Owns the 1,391-acre Big Cedar Industrial Center at Cedar Rapids, of which QTS took 612 acres.

contacts.role: Land brokerage and auctions; absorbed Murray Wise Associates
contacts.ask: What is under listing agreement but not yet marketed, and who holds a section or more of flat ground who would sell at the right number.
contacts.why: Large Iowa farms trade by auction and surface 30-60 days before sale, often never reaching listing sites.

contacts.role: Farm management and auctions, licensed in twelve states
contacts.ask: Unmarketed pipeline and farm-management clients with 500+ contiguous acres.
contacts.why: Farm managers know which owners are ageing out before any broker does.

contacts.org: Sullivan Auctioneers · Steffes Group · Farmers National · Iowa Land Company
contacts.role: Auction houses handling large Iowa farmland
contacts.ask: Pre-auction pipeline and private-treaty opportunities above 500 acres.
contacts.why: Three sites in the pipeline came from auction listings — these firms are already selling the ground being pursued.

contacts.org: Listing brokers already in the file
contacts.role: Brokers on two pipeline sites
contacts.ask: Not the listing they showed — what else they know of, and which owners nearby would sell at the right number.
contacts.why: Every land broker holds a mental list of large tracts whose owners are not formally selling.

contacts.role: Regional planning and economic development district
contacts.counties: Calhoun · Hamilton · Humboldt · Pocahontas · Webster · Wright
contacts.ask: Every site over 300 acres listed or not, current county zoning and data-centre ordinance status, and which cities have adopted 427B.
contacts.why: Covers six screen counties including Wright and Calhoun.

contacts.org: North Iowa Area Council of Governments
contacts.role: Regional planning and economic development district
contacts.counties: Cerro Gordo · Floyd · Franklin · Hancock · Kossuth · Mitchell · Winnebago · Worth
contacts.ask: Same three questions. Lead with Kossuth.
contacts.why: Covers Kossuth, the top-ranked county on the screen.

contacts.role: Regional planning and economic development district
contacts.counties: Buena Vista · Clay · Dickinson · Emmet · Lyon · O'Brien · Osceola · Palo Alto · Sioux
contacts.ask: Same three questions, plus whether Sioux County's moratorium has an expiry date on the record.
contacts.why: Covers two pipeline sites and the best landform counties in the state.

contacts.role: Regional planning and economic development district
contacts.ask: Same three questions. Lead with Cherokee and Ida.
contacts.why: Covers Cherokee, second on the screen, and Ida.

contacts.role: Regional planning and economic development district
contacts.ask: Same three questions, plus the acreage and flood footprint of the Iowa Falls industrial site.
contacts.why: Covers Hardin, where a pipeline site has no acreage recorded.

contacts.role: Regional planning and economic development district
contacts.counties: Audubon · Carroll · Crawford · Dallas · Greene · Guthrie · Sac
contacts.ask: Same three questions. Lead with Sac and Crawford.
contacts.why: Covers Sac and Crawford, both top-twelve on the screen.

contacts.org: Iowa Northland Regional Council of Governments
contacts.role: Regional planning and economic development district
contacts.counties: Black Hawk · Bremer · Buchanan · Butler · Chickasaw · Grundy
contacts.ask: Same three questions, and confirm in writing whether Chickasaw County has a countywide zoning ordinance.
contacts.why: Covers Grundy, and Chickasaw is one of the reported unzoned counties.

contacts.org: East Central Iowa Council of Governments
contacts.role: Regional planning and economic development district
contacts.counties: Benton · Iowa · Johnson · Jones · Linn · Washington
contacts.ask: Same three questions. Benton only — Linn and Johnson are closed.
contacts.why: Covers Benton. Iowa County and Washington County are both documented as unzoned or rescinded.

contacts.role: Regional planning and economic development district
contacts.counties: Adair · Adams · Clarke · Decatur · Madison · Ringgold · Taylor · Union
contacts.ask: Confirm the status of the Taylor County moratorium ordinance drafted 8 Jun 2026, and Ringgold County's current posture.
contacts.why: Covers four pipeline sites and both counties with live ordinance exposure.

contacts.role: Regional planning and economic development district
contacts.counties: Davis · Jefferson · Keokuk · Lucas · Mahaska · Monroe · Van Buren · Wapello · Wayne
contacts.ask: Same three questions for Davis County.
contacts.why: Covers two pipeline sites.

contacts.role: Regional planning and economic development district
contacts.counties: Cass · Fremont · Harrison · Mills · Montgomery · Page · Pottawattamie · Shelby
contacts.ask: Same three questions, plus what remains available at Mills Crossings Mega Site in Glenwood.
contacts.why: Covers Pottawattamie and Mills, home of the 1,600-acre certified mega site.

contacts.role: The only source for zoning status and ordinance posture
contacts.ask: Does the county have a countywide zoning ordinance? Is any data-centre ordinance or moratorium adopted or pending? What is the rezoning process and timeline for a 600-acre application?
contacts.why: Zoning status is the highest-leverage field in the dataset and the only one that cannot be downloaded.

contacts.role: Land brokerage — produced the first off-market lead in the project
contacts.ask: Anything else off-market at 500+ contiguous acres on ground outside the floodplain — and whether the Section 16 owners would consider an option rather than a sale.
contacts.why: Good first call. Surfaced a full 640-acre section where the owners have previously been willing to sell. The only warm owner-side lead on record.

contacts.role: Land brokerage
contacts.ask: Callback with any new inventory at 500+ contiguous acres. Nothing matching at present.
contacts.why: Answered; nothing that matches. Best available was 107 acres near Davenport — an order of magnitude too small. Asked to call back with changes.

contacts.role: Land brokerage
contacts.ask: Follow up by phone. A 2,700+ acre figure was noted against this firm and needs pinning to a location, a parcel count and an owner.
contacts.why: Contacted through the website, so no conversation yet. The largest acreage figure anywhere in the project sits against this firm and is entirely unqualified.

contacts.role: Land marketing and brokerage
contacts.ask: Awaiting callback. When it comes, lead with the acreage floor and the flat-ground requirement.
contacts.why: Said he will get back. Open thread.

contacts.role: Land brokerage — gave the clearest regional read of any contact so far
contacts.ask: Which specific central and northern counties he works, and what he has at 500+ acres with CSR2 in the 60s rather than the 80s.
contacts.why: Independently advised central or northern Iowa and described the southeast as too rough — matching the landform screen exactly, with no sight of it. Also anchors on CSR2 as the working metric, which is how the brokerage market prices ground.

contacts.role: Land auction house. Holds a November auction book and an Emmet County private sale
contacts.ask: Re-establish who this was. They hold a 1,300-acre auction on 1 Nov 2026, other large acreage auctions the same period, an Emmet County private sale around 500 acres, and offered to circulate off-market buyers.
contacts.why: The most productive single call in the log and the only one with no firm attached. Everything it produced is at risk of being unreachable.
